title: Replay: what the harness captured for one route on one exact game

name.description: The engine that replayed the route. godot and unity are game engines; a web page names its browser engine (harness/web/run.py writes chromium) or web when it does not record one. Each adapter in harness/adapters.py records which it writes.

seed.description: The seed the game's random stream was given (the route's). Unity only.

build.description: Unity only: the player that was replayed, named by the digest of what it was built from (harness/unity/run.py, build_key).

settle.description: Unity only: what ran before tick 0. ticks counts the physics ticks the game ran (the same on every run); frozenFrames counts frames held with Time.timeScale at 0 while a fade that runs on real time finished (it varies with the machine's speed, and no frame of it is captured).

hazards.description: Unity only: things the harness found that can make two replays differ.

integrity.description: Unity only: the exceptions and errors the game logged during the run (Application.logMessageReceived), counted, the first 50 listed.

isolation.description: What the game could reach while it ran (harness/sandbox.py). With a sandbox: no network, its own process tree, and a file system holding only its work copy, one output folder and its inputs. Without one, 'reason' says why and the game ran as the harness's user with only its environment narrowed. Written by the Godot harness; absent from older replays and from engines that do not record it yet, which a reader must treat as not isolated.

sandbox.description: The tool that isolated the game, or null when nothing did.

mode.description: What was asked for: isolate when possible, refuse to run without it, or do not isolate.

reason.description: Why the game was not isolated; null when it was.

processes.description: own: a separate process tree and /proc; host: the game could see the harness's processes.

environment.description: allowlist: only display and rendering variables were passed.

limits.description: Limits in force inside the sandbox, or null without one. Total disk use of the work copy and the output folder is not limited.
